Hey y'all! Just stopping by to introduce myself. I'm a stay-at-home, homeschooling mother of two boys. I live in Mississippi... Yeah, I think that part sucks too, but let's just get the bad stuff outta the way early. I'm 1/2 Yankee, just sayin'...

Now for the cool parts: I'm fluent in American Sign Language, play guitar, and I have an awesome pet squirrel.

I do lots of fun redneck things, like hand-grabbing catfish (some call it "noodling". Not me.) and frog-giggin' is our favorite. Basically, we take the boat to the swamp just after sunset and hunt bullfrogs until dawn. It's a ton of fun. And yes, it involves high levels of intoxication and an occasional water moccasin/cottonmouth in the boat. The best part is that you get to eat frog legs the next day. People, if you've never eaten deep-fried frog legs, you haven't lived.

Everytime I head down south I feel like I put on thirty pounds. Frog legs are so damn good.

Welcome aboard! What made you decide to homeschool?

I decided to homeschool my boys about 4 years ago. The schools here are just awful. I've seen high school "graduates" that could barely spell c-a-t. I'm an avid reader and I also love to write. I didn't want my children to grow up without the joy of losing themselves in a book. I didn't want them to be exposed to the violence in the school system here either. Just think of everything you've ever heard about Mississippi in general...

My children will be able to move anywhere they'd like to live and work when they are grown. They won't be chained to a life of factory work in the Mississippi Delta. They will have opportunities that I wasted. I want them to have a better life than I do.

Nice. I had always wished I could have homeschooled my son.

Does it impact their college chances at all?

Nope. If any thing, it actually improves their chances. Colleges/Universities have been scrambling to get home-schoolers. Home-schooled students out-perform public schoolers on almost any standardized test you can throw at them. My children are only in 5th & 6th grades, but already they read on a high-school level, write everything in the most beautiful cursive handwriting, and can hold an intelligent conversation with most any adult on most any topic.
Looks like this is my new home!
